title: GitHub - algebras-ai/algebras-agent
excerpt: Contribute to algebras-ai/algebras-agent development by creating an account on GitHub.
content_html:
Algebras Localization Agent

AI-powered localization workflow with automated QA and real-time fluency scoring via Algebras.

Works with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Windsurf, GitHub Copilot, or any agent that supports MCP tools.

AI agents: asked to localize a project with Algebras? Read AGENTS.md and follow it step by step. In short:

  1. Read the API key from ALGEBRAS_API_KEY (environment or .env).
  2. Connect the MCP server https://platform.algebras.ai/api/mcp with header x-api-key: <key>.
  3. Use the Project type: flow from plugin/PROJECT_TYPES.md (games, edtech, fintech, saas, or general).
  4. Run the workflow in plugin/CLAUDE.md: onboard → glossary → translate → qa.

Quick start

  1. Open platform.algebras.ai/translation/agent, create an API key, and save it as ALGEBRAS_API_KEY in your project's environment or .env.

  2. Open your repo in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Windsurf, Copilot, or any coding agent, and paste the prompt from that page:

    Localize this project with Algebras.
Follow the instructions in https://github.com/algebras-ai/algebras-agent
Use the API key from ALGEBRAS_API_KEY.
Project type: <games|edtech|fintech|saas|general>
Use the <type> flow from the agent instructions.

  3. The agent connects to Algebras, builds your localization context, translates, runs QA, and leaves the result on a new git branch (algebras/localize-<date>) for you to review like any other change.

To install the agent permanently in your tool instead (plugin or MCP config), see Install.

Project types

Type Use it for The flow emphasizes
games Games UI, quests, item names, lore
edtech Education products Lessons, quizzes, course pages
fintech Payments, banking, wallets, insurance Money states, fees, disclaimers, statements
saas Software products App UI, emails, help center
general Any other project Detected from your files, per file

Each flow is defined in plugin/PROJECT_TYPES.md.

Fluency checks

During onboarding the agent asks which fluency checks to run, and records the answer in project.json (add e.g. Fluency: context to the prompt to answer up front):

Setting What is scored Approx. cost per string of N words
none Nothing N
isolated A no-glossary translation, scored on its own (context-free) 2N + 10
context The written translation, scored with its neighbor strings and approved choices (context-aware) N + 10
both Both scores 2N + 20

Scores land in fluency_report.csv. They are a self-check of the agent's own translation, not an independent review.

Prepare your project folder

Put any brief, style guide, character list, glossary, or screenshots in the project folder next to the translation files. Any file name is fine — the agent classifies files by their contents. What to include, and which facts each target language forces, is in plugin/CONTEXT_REQUIREMENTS.md. Missing context doesn't block translation: the agent asks at most five questions and writes the rest to client_questions.md for you to forward to the client.

What the agent builds from your repo
Glossary Extracted from your code and UI strings, checked against established translations, and confirmed by you. Stored on the Algebras platform.
Translation memory Translations already in your repo are kept and reused as the reference for terminology and style. They aren't translated again.
Context files Specs, docs, lore and style guides found in your repo are classified by what they cover and read before glossary extraction and each translation batch.
Context facts Who speaks, to whom, formal or informal, what a placeholder stands for — recorded only from a cited source (context_pack.json, context_facts.jsonl). Open points go to client_questions.md, and the translation avoids committing to them.
Screenshots Screenshots already in your repo are linked to strings by column or file name and used as context. Automatic capture is coming soon.

Install

Claude Code

Note: Plugin commands require the Claude Code CLI (claude in your terminal). They are not available in the Claude Code web app or desktop app.

Run these commands in the Claude Code CLI from your project directory:

claude plugin marketplace add algebras-ai/algebras-agent
claude plugin install algebras-agent@algebras-agent

Then start an interactive session and run the setup skill — it opens your browser for the API key, copies workflow files into your project, and saves the key to .env:

claude

/algebras-agent:setup

The MCP server connects automatically once the plugin has your API key (declared in plugin.json). If you need to reconfigure the key later:

/plugin configure algebras-agent
/reload-plugins

Codex

Add the Algebras plugin marketplace, then install the plugin from Codex:

codex plugin marketplace add algebras-ai/algebras-agent
codex

Inside Codex, open the plugin browser:

/plugins

Install algebras-agent, then run the setup skill:

$setup

Restart Codex when prompted. You can verify the Algebras MCP server from:

/mcp

The plugin does not start the MCP server until setup saves your Algebras API key. If /mcp shows an unauthenticated algebras startup error from an earlier install, remove the old plugin install or delete the stale algebras MCP entry, run $setup, and restart Codex.

Cursor / Windsurf / Codex fallback

Run from your project root:

curl -fsSL https://platform.algebras.ai/install | bash

The script opens your browser for the API key, downloads the workflow files, and writes the MCP config automatically (.cursor/mcp.json, .windsurf/mcp.json, or ~/.codex/config.toml).

If your agent isn't auto-detected, pass --agent explicitly:

curl -fsSL https://platform.algebras.ai/install | bash -s -- --agent cursor
curl -fsSL https://platform.algebras.ai/install | bash -s -- --agent windsurf
curl -fsSL https://platform.algebras.ai/install | bash -s -- --agent codex

Translate

Once installed, open your project in your agent and send:

Translate this project.

Add a project type to pick a flow, e.g. Translate this project. Project type: saas. Or paste the full prompt from the Quick start — it works with or without the install step.

The agent onboards your project, builds a glossary, translates, and runs QA, asking you to confirm at each step. In a git repository it works on its own branch and commits the result at the end.

What's included

File Purpose
CLAUDE.md Workflow for Claude Code and Claude Desktop
AGENTS.md Workflow for OpenAI Codex / Agents
.cursorrules Workflow for Cursor
.windsurfrules Workflow for Windsurf
.github/copilot-instructions.md Workflow for GitHub Copilot
PROJECT_TYPES.md The games, edtech, fintech, saas and general flows
CONTEXT_REQUIREMENTS.md Client context the agent expects, the fact model, and which facts each target language forces
COMMON_MISTAKES.md Error taxonomy from real-world LQA
skills/<phase>/SKILL.md The phases: onboard, glossary, translate, qa, plus optional glossary-dedupe

AGENTS.md at the repository root is the entry point for agents that follow this repo's URL without installing anything.

GitHub Actions (CI/CD)

Automate translation in any repo's CI pipeline — no manual setup required.

Quick start

  1. Add these secrets in your repo: Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions

    Secret Value
    ALGEBRAS_API_KEY From platform.algebras.ai/api-keys
    ANTHROPIC_API_KEY From console.anthropic.com

  2. Copy .github/workflows/translate.example.yml from this repo into your project's .github/workflows/ and adjust the paths trigger to match your locale files.

  3. Push to main (or trigger via Actions → Translate → Run workflow).

What the action does

On each run the action:

  1. Downloads the latest workflow prompt files from this repo
  2. Checks project.json — exits early if all strings are already translated (skip-if-complete: true)
  3. Writes a temporary MCP config pointing to the Algebras platform
  4. Installs the Claude CLI and runs it non-interactively against your project
  5. The agent runs the full workflow: Onboard → Glossary → Translate → QA (skips phases that are already done)
  6. Detects changed files via git diff; commits and pushes (or opens a PR)

Inputs

Input Default Description
algebras-api-key — Required. Algebras API key
llm-provider anthropic anthropic or gemini
anthropic-api-key — Required if provider is anthropic
gemini-api-key — Required if provider is gemini
algebras-platform-url https://platform.algebras.ai Override for self-hosted
commit-changes true Commit translated files
create-pr false Open a PR instead of pushing directly
skip-if-complete true Exit early if nothing needs translating
project-type general Flow from PROJECT_TYPES.md: games, edtech, fintech, saas, or general
fluency isolated Fluency checks: none, isolated (context-free), context (context-aware), or both
min-fluency-score (empty) Fail if any string scores below this (1–10)

Example

- uses: algebras-ai/algebras-agent/.github/actions/algebras-translate@main
  with:
    algebras-api-key: ${{ secrets.ALGEBRAS_API_KEY }}
    anthropic-api-key: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
    commit-changes: "true"
    create-pr: "false"

Requirements

  • Python 3.10+ (for QA tools)
  • An Algebras account

content_html_zh:
Algebras Localization Agent

AI-powered localization workflow with automated QA and real-time fluency scoring via Algebras.

Works with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Windsurf, GitHub Copilot, or any agent that supports MCP tools.

AI agents: asked to localize a project with Algebras? Read AGENTS.md and follow it step by step. In short: Read the API key from ALGEBRAS_API_KEY (environment or .env). Connect the MCP server https://platform.algebras.ai/api/mcp with header x-api-key: <key>. Use the Project type: flow from plugin/PROJECT_TYPES.md (games, edtech, fintech, saas, or general). Run the workflow in plugin/CLAUDE.md: onboard → glossary → translate → qa.

快速启动

  1. Open platform.algebras.ai/translation/agent, create an API key, and save it as ALGEBRAS_API_KEY in your project's environment or .env.
  2. Open your repo in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Windsurf, Copilot, or any coding agent, and paste the prompt from that page: Localize this project with Algebras. Follow the instructions in https://github.com/algebras-ai/algebras-agent Use the API key from ALGEBRAS_API_KEY. Project type: <games|edtech|fintech|saas|general> Use the <type> flow from the agent instructions.
  3. The agent connects to Algebras, builds your localization context, translates, runs QA, and leaves the result on a new git branch (algebras/localize-<date>) for you to review like any other change.

To install the agent permanently in your tool instead (plugin or MCP config), see Install.

Project types

Type 用它来 The flow emphasizes
games Games UI, quests, item names, lore
edtech Education products Lessons, quizzes, course pages
fintech Payments, banking, wallets, insurance Money states, fees, disclaimers, statements
saas Software products App UI, emails, help center
一般的 Any other project Detected from your files, per file

Each flow is defined in plugin/PROJECT_TYPES.md.

Fluency checks

During onboarding the agent asks which fluency checks to run, and records the answer in project.json (add e.g. Fluency: context to the prompt to answer up front):

环境 What is scored 大约。 cost per string of N words
none 没有什么 N
孤立 A no-glossary translation, scored on its own (context-free) 2N + 10
语境 The written translation, scored with its neighbor strings and approved choices (context-aware) N + 10
both Both scores 2N + 20

Scores land in fluency_report.csv. They are a self-check of the agent's own translation, not an independent review.

Prepare your project folder

Put any brief, style guide, character list, glossary, or screenshots in the project folder next to the translation files. Any file name is fine — the agent classifies files by their contents. What to include, and which facts each target language forces, is in plugin/CONTEXT_REQUIREMENTS.md. Missing context doesn't block translation: the agent asks at most five questions and writes the rest to client_questions.md for you to forward to the client.

What the agent builds from your repo
词汇表 Extracted from your code and UI strings, checked against established translations, and confirmed by you. Stored on the Algebras platform.
Translation memory Translations already in your repo are kept and reused as the reference for terminology and style. They aren't translated again.
Context files Specs, docs, lore and style guides found in your repo are classified by what they cover and read before glossary extraction and each translation batch.
Context facts Who speaks, to whom, formal or informal, what a placeholder stands for — recorded only from a cited source (context_pack.json, context_facts.jsonl). Open points go to client_questions.md, and the translation avoids committing to them.
截图 Screenshots already in your repo are linked to strings by column or file name and used as context. Automatic capture is coming soon.

安装

克劳德·科德

Note: Plugin commands require the Claude Code CLI (claude in your terminal). They are not available in the Claude Code web app or desktop app.

Run these commands in the Claude Code CLI from your project directory:

claude plugin marketplace add algebras-ai/algebras-agent
claude plugin install algebras-agent@algebras-agent

Then start an interactive session and run the setup skill — it opens your browser for the API key, copies workflow files into your project, and saves the key to .env:

claude

/algebras-agent:setup

The MCP server connects automatically once the plugin has your API key (declared in plugin.json). If you need to reconfigure the key later:

/plugin configure algebras-agent
/reload-plugins

Codex

Add the Algebras plugin marketplace, then install the plugin from Codex:

codex plugin marketplace add algebras-ai/algebras-agent
codex

Inside Codex, open the plugin browser:

/plugins

Install algebras-agent, then run the setup skill:

$setup

Restart Codex when prompted. You can verify the Algebras MCP server from:

/mcp

The plugin does not start the MCP server until setup saves your Algebras API key. If /mcp shows an unauthenticated algebras startup error from an earlier install, remove the old plugin install or delete the stale algebras MCP entry, run $setup, and restart Codex.

Cursor / Windsurf / Codex fallback

Run from your project root:

curl -fsSL https://platform.algebras.ai/install | bash

The script opens your browser for the API key, downloads the workflow files, and writes the MCP config automatically (.cursor/mcp.json, .windsurf/mcp.json, or ~/.codex/config.toml).

If your agent isn't auto-detected, pass --agent explicitly:

curl -fsSL https://platform.algebras.ai/install | bash -s -- --agent cursor
curl -fsSL https://platform.algebras.ai/install | bash -s -- --agent windsurf
curl -fsSL https://platform.algebras.ai/install | bash -s -- --agent codex

Translate

Once installed, open your project in your agent and send:

Translate this project.

Add a project type to pick a flow, e.g. Translate this project. Project type: saas. Or paste the full prompt from the Quick start — it works with or without the install step.

The agent onboards your project, builds a glossary, translates, and runs QA, asking you to confirm at each step. In a git repository it works on its own branch and commits the result at the end.

What's included

File 目的
CLAUDE.md Workflow for Claude Code and Claude Desktop
AGENTS.md Workflow for OpenAI Codex / Agents
.cursorrules Workflow for Cursor
.windsurfrules Workflow for Windsurf
.github/copilot-instructions.md Workflow for GitHub Copilot
PROJECT_TYPES.md The games, edtech, fintech, saas and general flows

AGENTS.md at the repository root is the entry point for agents that follow this repo's URL without installing anything.

GitHub Actions (CI/CD)

Automate translation in any repo's CI pipeline — no manual setup required.

快速启动

  1. Add these secrets in your repo: Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions Secret Value ALGEBRAS_API_KEY From platform.algebras.ai/api-keys ANTHROPIC_API_KEY From console.anthropic.com
  2. Copy .github/workflows/translate.example.yml from this repo into your project's .github/workflows/ and adjust the paths trigger to match your locale files.
  3. Push to main (or trigger via Actions → Translate → Run workflow).

What the action does

On each run the action:

  1. Downloads the latest workflow prompt files from this repo
  2. Checks project.json — exits early if all strings are already translated (skip-if-complete: true)
  3. Writes a temporary MCP config pointing to the Algebras platform
  4. Installs the Claude CLI and runs it non-interactively against your project
  5. The agent runs the full workflow: Onboard → Glossary → Translate → QA (skips phases that are already done)
  6. Detects changed files via git diff; commits and pushes (or opens a PR)

输入

Input 默认 描述
algebras-api-key — 必需的。 Algebras API key
llm-provider 人择的 anthropic or gemini
anthropic-api-key — Required if provider is anthropic
gemini-api-key — Required if provider is gemini
algebras-platform-url https://platform.algebras.ai Override for self-hosted
commit-changes true Commit translated files
create-pr false Open a PR instead of pushing directly
skip-if-complete true Exit early if nothing needs translating
project-type 一般的 Flow from PROJECT_TYPES.md: games, edtech, fintech, saas, or general
fluency 孤立 Fluency checks: none, isolated (context-free), context (context-aware), or both
min-fluency-score (empty) Fail if any string scores below this (1–10)

例子

- uses: algebras-ai/algebras-agent/.github/actions/algebras-translate@main
  with:
    algebras-api-key: ${{ secrets.ALGEBRAS_API_KEY }}
    anthropic-api-key: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
    commit-changes: "true"
    create-pr: "false"

要求

  • Python 3.10+ (for QA tools)
  • An Algebras account
